Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:
Facilitation; Productowner

Stellenbeschreibung:
Programme & Community Developer Berlin · 32–36 hrs/week · Starting September/October 2026 or by arrangement · fixed on-site times: 3–4 evenings + 1 weekend day

⚠️ Important – please read first: This position is funded exclusively through § 16e SGB II. You can only apply if you meet this funding requirement: **at least 21 of the last 24 months receiving Jobcenter benefits (Bürgergeld/SGB II).**Please note: time with the Agentur für Arbeit (unemployment benefit / Arbeitslosengeld I) does NOT count – only benefits received through the Jobcenter count. If you're unsure whether you qualify, it's best to check quickly with your Jobcenter contact before applying.

About ForEveryone ForEveryone is a non-profit social enterprise in Berlin. We bring people from different backgrounds together, among other things through our community café at Boxhagener Platz and through workshops, events and activities for an international Berlin audience. We are growing, and we are currently reshaping our whole range of activities.

What this role is about We are looking for someone to oversee, develop and be present across our whole range of activities – from workshops to events at our community café at Boxhagener Platz (jam sessions, music nights, exhibitions and more). The clear goal: turning individual activities into recurring small communities with their own memberships. Instead of activities we have to market and fill again every time, we want formats people come back to regularly – a knitting club, a sports format, creative combinations, a recurring music night. You drive this: you sense what the community wants, develop formats to match, test them, run them yourself, recruit and support the volunteers who help carry them, and make sure the good ones actually happen and grow.

What you'll do

- Oversee and support the offering. You keep an eye on all running activities – workshops and café events alike – are regularly present on site, and make sure everything runs smoothly, including the operational side in our booking tool (cancellations, refunds, correct details) – a small but important part of the week.
- Develop and test formats and events. You sense what activities the community wants, identify new workshop, event and mini-formats, research trends and seasonal demand (what are others offering, what works in a summer lull?), and honestly test which formats land well enough to sustain, and which don't.
- Build mini-communities with memberships. You develop formats with recurring communities in mind – ones people belong to as members – and take them from first idea to an established, recurring offering.
- Run activities and enable volunteers. You run workshops and events yourself on a regular basis, at a good standard – weekly, sometimes with support from volunteers. You recruit volunteers (including from among participants), onboard them, give them direct feedback, and support them until they can carry a format.
- Guide formats through their phases. For new formats: experiment and learn from feedback. For established ones: set up clean processes, with reliability and scaling in mind.

What you bring

- Experience running workshops, events, groups or community formats, at a quality others can build on.
- A feel for people and communities, and enjoyment in recruiting and supporting volunteers.
- Conceptual strength: you can develop formats, test them, and judge honestly what works.
- Self-direction and ownership – you drive your area like a genuine project lead.
- Fixed on-site times: at least 3–4 evenings per week (around 2–3 hours each, within the 5–10 pm window) plus 1 day at the weekend (Saturday or Sunday, daytime or evening). These are your core working hours. The rest of your time you can arrange flexibly from the office. This on-site presence comes with a lot of creative freedom, but it is also a clear expectation.
- Comfortable with digital tools; German and English are a strong plus for our multilingual community.

What to expect from us

- A role with real room to shape things: you are building something that doesn't exist yet.
- A small, committed team and real closeness to a lively, international community.
- We set the strategic and financial direction (e.g. the membership model) as managing directors; you develop and decide on the formats independently, with our final sign-off.

Terms

- Hours: 32–36 per week
- Start: September/October 2026 or by arrangement
- Pay: €2,400–2,800 gross/month (at 36 hrs)
- Location: Coworking Kiezlab, Berlin · hybrid

jobs.description:
Summary

Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. Smart people and inspiring, innovative technologies are the norms here. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? Are you ready to be part of a team redefining cellular wireless technology? Join us to help deliver the next groundbreaking Apple product. In this role, you will be a key member of our team working on the RF/Analog layout of integrated cellular RF transceivers in innovative RF CMOS technologies.

Description

Floor-planning in collaboration with RF IC design and RF system team. The layout of RF, analog, and digital blocks for RF ICs down to the transistor level. Block-level and top-level layout through full verification flow. Top-level layout integration, verification, and schedule management. Work with packaging experts to simulate RF de-sense and coupling mechanisms. Layout reviews for routing, signal path, IQ matching, and coupling.

Minimum Qualifications

- Very good proficiency in the interpretation of CALIBRE DRC, LVS, ANTENNA-DRC, etc.
- Knowledge of CADENCE layout tools
- English language fluency is required for this position

Preferred Qualifications

- The ideal candidate will have 5+ years of custom RF/analog layout experience with extensive knowledge of deep sub-micron CMOS and FinFET technologies
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, and a minimum of 3 years relevant industry experience 
- Knowledge of layout techniques for device matching, parasitics reduction, RF shielding, and efficient high-frequency routing
- Proven understanding of RF building blocks such as LNAs, mixers, VCOs, DCOs, PAs, etc.
- Good understanding of RC delay, electro-migration, and coupling effects
- High-level proficiency in the interpretation of CALIBRE DRC, LVS, ANTENNA-DRC, etc.
- Excellent communication skills and ability to work in multi-functional teams
- Experience in working with international teams

As a Machine Learning Compiler Engineer on the Apple Neural Engine (ANE) team, you'll work to bring high-performance, low-power AI solutions to life on iconic Apple products like the Vision Pro, iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more. - Familiarity with Just-in-Time (JIT) compilation and dynamic optimization techniques for real-time code execution

A job is more than just a job. It should be the right fit for you, challenge you, and offer fair compensation. That's exactly how we see it at PAMEC. We connect you with companies that truly match your skills, goals, and ambitions. When you love your job, we know we've done ours right – and we've been doing just that since 1984.

For our renowned client, a leading international corporation, we are looking for a Approval Engineer (gn) for Connected Products.

This is what your day-to-day work will look like

- Growing demands development projects require timely executions of worldwide approvals for our devices
- Coordination with our marketing and product development teams
- Create approval concepts and coordinate approval activities with external bodies
- Close collaboration with international locations, suppliers, development partners and international test and approval institutes

What makes you a great fit

- A university degree in electrical engineering, information technology, mechatronics, or related discipline

- Strong teamwork and communication skills
- A collaborative mindset combined with a high degree of independent decision-making
- Analytical abilities, a proactive approach, and entrepreneurial thinking and behavior

- Permanent employment contract with the opportunity for a long-term position at our partner company

- Employee referral bonus of up to € 400 through our "Refer a Friend" program

Stellenbeschreibung:
Start: asap

As a Bike Mechanic, you’ll be responsible for the complete repair and refurbishment of e-bikes, ensuring each one meets the highest quality standards before being delivered to customers. You’ll work with a dedicated and skilled team in a fully equipped workshop using state-of-the-art tools and diagnostic equipment.

Your Role

- Independently perform inspection, troubleshooting, spare parts selection, repair, and quality control on a wide variety of e-bikes.
- Prepare e-bikes for customer delivery and maintain the in-house fleet.
- Contribute to continuous improvement in repair processes and service quality.
- Support warehouse operations with ideas to optimize efficiency and workflow.

Your Qualifications

- 1–2 years of experience in bike or e-bike mechanics (2+ years for Senior Mechanic).
- Solid knowledge of electric bikes, their components, and diagnostic tools.
- Passion for quality, efficiency, and hands-on technical problem-solving.
- Comfort working independently and as part of a close-knit team.
- Fluency in English or  German

The Offer

- A permanent employment contract with a competitive monthly salary.
- Monday to Friday schedule – your weekends are always free.
- Opportunity to work with a huge variety of e-bikes, from almost-new to heavily used.
- Modern workshop environment with electric stands, high-end tools, and advanced diagnostic systems.
- Regular performance reviews every 6 months with promotion opportunities.
- A team of experienced mechanics who support your growth and share their expertise.
- A dynamic and supportive startup culture with real room for personal development and impact.

HR Coordinator

International SOS is the world’s leading medical and security services company with over 12,000 employees working in 1,000 locations in 90 countries. International SOS Government Services administers the TRICARE Overseas Program providing high-quality, accessible health care services for U.S. Military service members, family members, retirees, and other eligible beneficiaries overseas.

About the role

Stuttgart, Germany | Hybrid working – two days from home

Join International SOS Government Services and play a key role in supporting the people behind the TRICARE Overseas Program; an international healthcare program serving military communities overseas.

As the HR point of contact for our Stuttgart office, you will partner with managers and employees across Germany and the wider region, providing trusted advice throughout the employee lifecycle.

Key responsibilities

- Act as the first point of contact for HR matters in Stuttgart, building trusted relationships with employees, managers and senior leaders
- Provide practical guidance on employee relations, performance management, probation, contract changes, rewards, investigations, mediation, disciplinary processes and terminations
- Deliver a welcoming and engaging onboarding experience, including induction presentations and follow-up evaluations
- Work with colleagues to validate monthly payroll changes and ensure information is accurate and submitted on time
- Review HR data, metrics and workforce trends to provide useful insights and support business decisions
- Contribute to HR and organisational development projects across European operations
- Identify opportunities to improve HR processes, solve problems and make services more effective
- Manage sensitive HR correspondence with professionalism, accuracy and discretion

About you

- 3–5 years of HR experience, ideally in a multicultural, matrix organisation
- Strong HR operations, coordination and advisory experience
- Good knowledge of German employment law and Works Council collaboration
- Excellent communication, relationship-building and organisational skills
- Confidence working independently and managing multiple priorities
- Fluent German and English
- MS Office 365 and HRIS experience; SuccessFactors or ADP would be an advantage
- Professional HR certification is desirable but not essential

Occasional travel within the EU may be required.

Ready to make an impact in a fast-moving international healthcare programme? Join TRICARE and help create an exceptional employee experience for the teams delivering essential support across Europe.

By joining International SOS, you will contribute to a global network dedicated to protecting people and organisations. We offer a dynamic and respectful workplace where expertise, innovation, and collaboration drive our success. International SOS has been awarded as a Top Employer in the UK by the Top Employer’s Institute (TEI) for 2025.

13,000 experts | 1,200+ locations | 90 countries | 110+ languages

Start your journey with us today. Apply now!

Senior Electrical Systems Engineer (m/f/d)

Instrumentation, Controls & Power Systems

Help Accelerate Industrial Decarbonization

Join exceptional people from around the world to solve some of the world's toughest energy challenges, make a real impact, and enjoy the adventure of building the future of industrial decarbonization together.

As our Senior Electrical Systems Engineer (m/f/d) – Instrumentation, Controls & Power Systems, you will play a key role in designing the electrical infrastructure that powers GlassPoint's next generation of solar thermal plants.

Working closely with colleagues across Mechanical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Systems Engineering, EPC partners, and suppliers, you will develop safe, reliable, and efficient electrical solutions for industrial-scale renewable energy facilities.

From concept development through commissioning, you'll contribute to projects that are shaping the future of industrial heat and energy.

Your Impact

In this role, you'll design electrical systems that enable the safe and efficient operation of some of the world's largest solar thermal facilities, supporting heavy industry on its journey toward decarbonization.

You'll combine technical expertise with systems thinking, working with internal teams, EPC partners, and global suppliers to develop robust, scalable electrical solutions that become part of our commercial projects worldwide.

What You'll Do

Design Electrical Systems

- Develop the conceptual design of electrical systems for solar thermal plants.
- Design and specify electrical heat tracing (EHT) systems, including piping, tanks, cable routing, junction boxes, and interfaces to plant control systems.
- Develop electrical architectures that support reliable, efficient, and safe plant operation.
- Ensure compliance with applicable international standards, regulations, and engineering best practices.

Develop Instrumentation & Control Systems

- Specify instrumentation including temperature, pressure, flow, and level measurement devices.
- Collaborate with Controls Engineering teams to define automation concepts, control philosophies, and system interfaces.
- Develop instrumentation and control (I&C) architectures for molten-salt solar thermal systems.
- Support the development of tracking algorithms, automation solutions, and electrical control strategies.

Engineering & Supplier Collaboration

- Select and specify electrical drive systems for solar collector tracking.
- Prepare technical specifications and tender documentation.
- Evaluate supplier solutions and support technical decision-making.
- Collaborate with engineering partners, control system providers, and equipment vendors throughout the project lifecycle.
- Manage technical interfaces and support successful project execution.

Support Project Delivery

- Support prototype development, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting.
- Work collaboratively across disciplines to resolve technical challenges.
- Contribute to the development and improvement of electrical design standards and engineering processes.
- Provide technical expertise throughout all project phases, from concept development through commissioning.

Who You Are

You enjoy solving complex engineering challenges and designing reliable systems for demanding industrial environments. You combine strong technical expertise with a practical, solution-oriented mindset and have experience managing external partners and vendors. You thrive in multidisciplinary teams, communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and balance attention to detail with system-level thinking. Curious, collaborative, and eager to learn, you enjoy helping build engineering processes in a growing technology company while working both independently and as part of a team.

Ideally, you'll bring

- Master's degree (or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field.
- Several years of experience designing electrical systems for industrial plants, renewable energy projects, power generation facilities, or process industries.
- Strong experience in electrical engineering, instrumentation, and control system design.
- Experience designing or specifying electrical heat tracing (EHT) systems and associated electrical infrastructure.
- Solid understanding of electrical power distribution and component selection.
- Experience with electrical drives, motors, and motion systems.
- Knowledge of industrial instrumentation, including temperature, pressure, flow, and level measurement technologies.
- Experience with process wiring, cable design, and electrical documentation.
- Understanding of low-voltage protection concepts and electrical safety principles.
- Experience creating technical documentation such as P&IDs, loop diagrams, and equipment specifications.
- Familiarity with international engineering standards such as IEC and VDE; knowledge of NEC is beneficial.
- Experience with PLC programming, industrial automation, or control software would be an advantage.
- Interest in microprocessor-based systems and edge controllers.
- Experience working with suppliers, contractors, or external engineering partners.
- Strong communication skills in English; German language skills are welcome but not required.

What You'll Find at GlassPoint

- Meaningful work that contributes directly to global decarbonization efforts with opportunities to take ownership and make an impact from day one.
- An inclusive, collaborative, and international working environment.
- Colleagues who support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate success together.
- Challenging projects that encourage innovation, growth, and continuous learning.
- The chance to help scale a technology that is transforming how heavy industry generates heat and steam.

At GlassPoint, we believe that different perspectives drive innovation and strengthen our teams. We are committed to providing an inclusive working environment where everyone is treated with respect, feels valued, and has the opportunity to contribute their best work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, ethnic or social background, nationality, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We have zero tolerance for discrimination, harassment, bullying, or retaliation.

If you require reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, we encourage you to let us know.
